findings.issue: The 2026 journal editorial describes a planned journal-specific requirement for examples of substantive AI use; the current publisher policy and the editorial differ on copy-editing disclosure.
findings.resolution: Retain the applicable publisher disclosure and advise checking the current journal instructions for any newly implemented journal-specific requirement; editorial describes this as planned, not established. Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00426-026-02246-0.

findings.issue: The journal prohibits AI-written original text even though it permits disclosed analytical assistance.
findings.resolution: Retain the prohibited manuscript drafting classification and exclude from the compatible main directory. https://spb.psychopen.eu/index.php/spb/policies

notes: Reviewed all 18 candidate records and the fee, geography and AI policy patches. Independent official source checks included Sage journal instructions, Springer journal homepages and AI guidance, and PsychOpen policies; a role review is not human scientific review.
Prior metrics are retained with their original source, date and population rather than replaced with empty arrays. No inferred acceptance rates or subjective difficulty bands.

Springer exploratory analysis and author-led drafting guidance supports conditional compatibility under the campaign semantic rule; some article or use restrictions remain. Sage policy prohibits GenAI analysis of experiences or themes, limiting appropriate applications.
Sage journal instructions affirm worldwide authorship, and Current Psychology explicitly encourages authors worldwide; this does not eliminate other author or manuscript requirements.
Publisher journal homepages show no impact factor for Computational Brain & Behavior at the time checked; no missing metric is inferred.
